title: DNA replication
examples: What is the role of DNA polymerase in replication?
How does the Meselson–Stahl experiment prove semi-conservative replication?
Can you explain the difference between leading and lagging strand synthesis?

explain.say: DNA replication must copy the entire DNA molecule before cell division.
The process is semi-conservative, meaning each new DNA molecule has two old strands.
Special proteins called enzymes are needed to build the new DNA strands correctly.
The Meselson–Stahl experiment used density gradients to track the DNA strands.
In real life, when your body cells divide, this process ensures that all new cells get a full set of DNA.
A common mistake is forgetting that synthesis only happens in one direction on the strand.

faq.q: What does semi-conservative replication actually mean for the DNA molecule?
faq.a: It means that when DNA copies itself, each new copy keeps one original strand and builds a complementary new strand.
asks: Does the old DNA stay in the new DNA?

faq.q: Which enzyme is primarily responsible for adding the new nucleotides during replication?
faq.a: DNA polymerase is the main enzyme that synthesizes the new DNA strands by adding nucleotides to the existing template.

faq.q: What was the main conclusion from the Meselson–Stahl experiment?
faq.a: The experiment proved that DNA replication is semi-conservative because the DNA density changed predictably across generations.
asks: What did the N15 and N14 isotopes show?
How did they prove the mechanism?

faq.q: Why is the direction of synthesis important to remember?
faq.a: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides in the five prime to three prime direction, which dictates how the two strands are copied.
asks: Is synthesis always in one direction?

faq.q: Do all parts of the DNA molecule replicate at the same time?
faq.a: Generally, the entire molecule replicates together, but the physical process involves different mechanisms for the leading and lagging strands.
asks: Does replication happen all at once?

facts: DNA replication is a semi-conservative process.
DNA polymerase is the key enzyme for synthesizing new DNA strands.
The Meselson–Stahl experiment used heavy and light nitrogen isotopes.
Synthesis of new DNA strands always proceeds in the five prime to three prime direction.

quiz.say: If the parent DNA was entirely heavy (N15), what color/density will the DNA after the first round of replication be?
quiz.why: Semi-conservative replication means one old strand (heavy) pairs with one new strand (light), resulting in a hybrid density.

wrong.0: This is the correct answer, showing a mix of heavy and light components.
wrong.2: This would imply the new strand was also heavy, which is incorrect because the template strand is old.
wrong.3: This would mean the original heavy strand was somehow replaced entirely by light material.

quiz.say: When synthesizing a new strand, which direction must DNA polymerase add the nucleotides?
quiz.why: DNA polymerase has a specific enzymatic requirement to only add nucleotides in the direction moving from the five prime end to the three prime end.

wrong.1: The enzyme cannot synthesize DNA in this reverse direction.
wrong.2: The process is highly regulated and directional, not random.
wrong.3: While the leading strand is continuous, the rule applies to the chemical mechanism itself.

quiz.say: What does the term 'semi-conservative' tell us about the original DNA molecule?

options.show: It is discarded after replication is complete.
options.say: It is discarded after replication is complete.

options.show: It serves as a template for the new strand.
options.say: It serves as a template for the new strand.

options.show: It is completely broken down into nucleotides.
options.say: It is completely broken down into nucleotides.

options.show: It is chemically altered to match the new strand.
options.say: It is chemically altered to match the new strand.

quiz.why: The original strands provide the sequence information, acting as a template, but they are not incorporated into the new strand's structure.

wrong.0: The original strands are essential components of the resulting double helix.
wrong.2: If it broke down completely, there would be no template to guide the new synthesis.
wrong.3: The original strand remains chemically intact, serving only as a guide.
